stances.summary: Questions whether vulnerable Medicaid patients can navigate work requirement process
stances.quote: Will a Medicaid enrollee who suffers from seizures and addiction, and became homeless after losing his job, be able to navigate the process to prove he's too frail to work? That's the kind of question hanging over the implementation of a new Medicaid work requirement. @k-hought.b

stances.summary: Medicare for All easier to explain than incremental ACA reforms
stances.quote: Medicare for All is the only health reform policy that truly fits on a bumper sticker. Incremental policies are inherently more complicated to explain. The ACA did much more than ban pre-existing condition exclusions, but that part was easy for people to grasp.

stances.summary: Expiring ACA subsidies causing patients unable to pay hospital bills
New Mexico's state subsidy replacement uniquely sustained ACA enrollment
stances.quote:
ACA enrollment has dropped in every state, except New Mexico. What's special about New Mexico? They are the only state to fully replace the extra federal premium subsidies that ended this year.

stances.summary: CBO projects uninsured rate to exceed 10 percent after subsidies expire
stances.quote:
New: With enhanced ACA premium subsidies expired and Medicaid cuts phasing in, the Congressional Budget Office expects the share of the population uninsured to rise above 10% for the first time since the ACA was implemented.
www.cbo.gov/publication/...

stances.summary: Medicaid computer system errors reflect broader health insurance complexity problem
stances.quote: A story from our news operation about patients getting caught up in errors in Medicaid computer systems, operated by a private contractor. This is a symptom of a health insurance system that has become mind-numbingly complex.

stances.summary: Medicare for All could reduce health spending, redistribute costs from premiums to taxes

stances.summary: Highlights that ACA enrollees concentrate in Trump-won states
stances.quote: This is a remarkable statistic: 18.7 million out of the 24.3 million Obamacare enrollees are in states won by President Trump in 2024. https://t.co/xC5XAdzOpr

stances.summary: Clarifies Medicaid as health insurance, not welfare assistance
stances.quote: Most adults on Medicaid already work, because you can't use Medicaid to pay your rent or your grocery bills. It's health insurance that pays your medical bills if you get sick.

stances.summary: Defends Medicaid as essential coverage for low-wage workers
stances.quote: Low-income workers who are covered by Medicaid are generally in jobs that don't provide health benefits. Without Medicaid, they'd be uninsured.

stances.summary: Questions DOGE scrutiny of overpayment to Medicare Advantage plans
stances.quote: Have the @DOGE folks made it to the part of the system yet that shows private Medicare Advantage plans get paid by the government 22% more than costs would be in traditional Medicare?

stances.summary: Signals Medicare for All will become prominent campaign issue if El-Sayed wins
stances.quote: If Abdul El-Sayed wins the Michigan senate primary next week, I suspect we're going to be talking a lot more about Medicare for All.
